description: Bidirectional mapping between Magnetic schema components and documented Harbor Elements context nodes.

magnetic.catalog: component nodes and Figma library sets

triggers: The Magnetic schema package version changes.
The Harbor Elements context package version changes.
A Magnetic component node or Figma library set is added, removed, or renamed.
A mapped Harbor context node or public API changes.
checks: Compare the complete Magnetic component catalog with mappings[].magneticNode.
Validate every figmaTargets value against the current Magnetic Create catalog.
Validate every harborContextNodes value against the current Elements context map.
Review context-gap entries for newly documented Harbor targets.
Run the component-map and installer tests.

sourcePriority: Magnetic Create reference or block as supplemental guidance

contextDocumentPolicy.rule: After the agent selects a Harbor context node, it must read that node's shared and framework usage documents before it generates code. This rule also applies when Figma metadata identifies a Harbor-only primitive.

figmaMetadata.rule: Write this metadata on every Magnetic-style primitive that represents a Harbor-only component. Preserve the source properties as JSON in sourceProps.

semanticResolution: Treat hbr-link as navigation or download content.
Treat every hbr-button, including a link-styled or text variant, as an action button.
Never map hbr-link to Magnetic button only because both can have fill, outline, or text styling.
Map the outer documented component before its internal Shadow DOM components.
Use an attached Magnetic member when the parent component owns that member.
Do not create a duplicate standalone component for an attached member.
codeToFigma: Use the requested viewport width only.
Extend the frame height to include the full vertical scroll content.
Load content that appears during vertical scrolling.
Render each fixed or sticky element once.
Use the selected Magnetic Figma target when a documented mapping exists.
Render a Magnetic-style primitive when a Harbor-only component has no Magnetic target.
Add figmaMetadata to every Harbor-only primitive.
Use blocks as flexible starting points. Adapt their structure to the user's request.
figmaToCode: Read Magnetic instance data and Harbor figmaMetadata before visual inference.
Use structured Figma design context as the source for spacing. Use screenshots only for visual validation.
Record Auto Layout direction, wrapping, item gaps, four padding values, alignment, sizing, and child layout behavior before code generation.
Let explicit Figma spacing override generic code-generation spacing defaults.
Map Figma Auto Layout to flex or grid layout before considering absolute positioning.
Use scoped layout-only CSS when Harbor layout properties cannot express an explicit Figma value.
Do not override Harbor component internals to force a spacing match. Report a component parity gap.
Verify computed padding and gap values at the source viewport.
Resolve the mapping and its Harbor context nodes.
Read the selected Harbor context usage documents before code generation.
Use the detected framework and installation profile.
Preserve interaction semantics, content, state, hierarchy, and accessibility intent.
Do not generate a Harbor component when the mapping has context-gap status. Report the missing context document.
fromScratchToCode: Read this map before selecting Harbor application components.
Infer the Magnetic component job from the user's goal, interaction, content, and data shape.
Select the mapping entry whose magneticNode, figmaTargets, and selection rule match that job.
Use harborContextNodes to locate the Harbor implementation documents.
Read every selected Harbor usage document before generating code.
Treat blocks and component families as flexible starting points, not fixed output structures.
Do not generate a Harbor component when the mapping has context-gap status. Report the missing context document.
notification: Map a standalone Harbor notification indicator to Magnetic badge.
Use a status icon inside notification banners.
Keep the status icon attached to the banner.
cards: Map hbr-card with container to container-card.
Map a non-container card with one status or KPI to status-card.
Map a non-container card with a value and trend or delta to statistics-card.
Map a non-container card with related health measures to health-card.
Map every other non-container card to basic-card.
Do not infer container-card from visual complexity when the source hbr-card does not use container.
Do not nest a container card inside another container card.

mappings.selection: Map the timeline and its panels as one activity timeline composition.
Use this mapping only for in-page anchor navigation. Map the complete composition, not each child as a standalone component.
Use for counts, dots, and indicators attached to another object. Do not use it as a status icon inside a banner.
Select the specialized target from content shape. Keep every target in the non-container hbr-card family.
Preserve item order and the current page semantics.
Use for actions. A link-styled or text hbr-button remains a button. It does not become hbr-link.
Generate a documented group of related action buttons.
Select the chart type from the data relationship and the documented Harbor chart node.
Use the group target only when the controls form one named selection group.
Preserve code content, language intent, line numbers, and copy behavior.
Use hbr-accordion for the equivalent progressive-disclosure behavior. Preserve open state and grouping.
Generate hbr-card with container. Preserve standard, left-title, or collapsible intent when the documents support it.
Preserve the copied value and its accessible label.
Generate hbr-input with type datetime-local after reading the input document.
Generate hbr-input with type date.
Preserve orientation and grouping purpose.
Preserve header, body, footer, open state, and modal behavior.
Map the trigger and menu as one dropdown. Do not emit its internal buttons as separate top-level components.
Treat hbr-illustration as the illustration member of the empty state when it appears in that context.
Use only for anchored feature-discovery content. Never map hbr-highlight to this component.
Preserve fixed filters, overflow filters, search, result count, and actions.
Generate a documented hbr-button with floating behavior. Keep button action semantics.
Use links for navigation and legal destinations. Use buttons only for footer actions.
Map the complete shell header before its internal actions and menus.
Use an inline hbr-banner composition. Keep its status icon and optional link attached to the banner.
Use input-autocomplete only when suggestions exist. hbr-highlight can mark query matches inside suggestion content.
Keep value links as links. Map them as attached content when the Figma target supports them.
The installed Harbor context has no documented map component. Do not generate a Harbor component until a context node exists.
Preserve axes, cell state, labels, and controls described by the Matrix documents.
Map modal and overlay as one interaction. Preserve title, body, footer, size, and close behavior.
Use for the expanded drawer area of shell navigation.
Map the complete primary navigation structure before its internal items.
Generate hbr-input with type number and preserve range and step values.
Use page placement and message scope to distinguish it from inline and product-level banners.
Select one documented page-title pattern. Do not mix every optional pattern into one title.
Map hbr-pagination as one component. Ignore its internal hbr-link Shadow DOM implementation.
Generate hbr-input with type password and preserve password-toggle intent.
Use the default popover for contextual anchored content. Keep navigation links and action buttons semantically distinct.
Use only for persistent product-wide messages below the shell header.
Select determinate progress, indeterminate spinner, or skeleton from the source loading state.
Preserve percentage, label, and sentiment.
Use hbr-radio for standard radio controls. Do not substitute the button-styled hbr-radio-button.
Harbor Elements contains this component, but the installed context package has no usage document. Do not generate it until the context node exists.
Use search input behavior. Use hbr-highlight only for matching query text in results or suggestions.
Map input and menu as one select. Use hbr-highlight only for query matches inside searchable options.
Generate the documented Harbor skeleton classes and layout. There is no hbr-skeleton custom element in the context document.
Preserve range, current value, steps, marks, and disabled state.
Use for indeterminate progress. Keep an attached button spinner inside its button.
Select stepped-modal only when the workflow is modal. Otherwise use stepper-container.
Preserve placement in its form or page scope and preserve action order.
Use the documented horizontal primary-tab composition.
Use the documented horizontal secondary-tab composition.
Preserve vertical orientation and selected state.
Map documented cell semantics. Detailed table and long-collection generation guidance is intentionally deferred.
Preserve category or status purpose, sentiment, selection, and removal behavior.
Preserve semantic text role before exact visual size.
Preserve label, help, validation, resize, and value behavior.
Generate hbr-input with type time after reading the input document.
Use transient overlay placement to distinguish a toast from an inline banner. Keep status icon and optional link attached.
Preserve immediate on-off behavior, label, help, and disabled state.
Keep tooltip text short and associate it with one trigger.
Preserve source and destination lists, selection, movement actions, and empty state.
Harbor Elements contains these components, but the installed context package has no standalone tree usage document. Do not generate them until the context node exists.
Select button trigger or drag-and-drop from the source interaction. Preserve file state and restrictions.
Use hbr-radio-button only as the button-styled child of hbr-view-switcher.

harborOnlyAndAttached.rule: Use for matched query text in components such as search, select, autocomplete, and input results. Do not map it to Magnetic feature-highlight.
Use an attached parent link member when available. Otherwise render a Magnetic-style text-link primitive with metadata. Never convert it to Magnetic button or hbr-button.
Map anchor navigation to anchor-link-menu. Render every other documented list as flexible Magnetic-style text and layout primitives with metadata.
Keep the item inside its list. Preserve nesting, active state, disabled state, and prefix or suffix content.
Use the attached Magnetic empty-state illustration when the illustration belongs to an empty state. Use a metadata-bearing primitive when it is standalone.
